channel.title: Orchard
channel.description: Apple news, rumors and iPhone Duo apps, each with its source. An independent site, not affiliated with Apple.

item.title: iOS 27.2.1 and matching updates for Mac, Watch and Vision Pro are out
item.description: Apple released iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 with bug fixes and security updates, alongside macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1. Security-focused updates also went out for older systems: iOS and iPadOS 26.7.3 and 18.7.12, watchOS 26.6.1, and macOS 26.7.3 and 15.8.3 (the last two…

item.title: Apple starts selling $49.99 'intelligence usage packs'
item.description: Apple's first paid AI add-on gives extra use of select AI features once you hit your monthly limit. It is a one-time purchase, not a subscription, and for now it is offered only in Logic Pro. Packs don't work with Family Sharing, and unused usage expires 12 months after purchase. 9to5Mac says…

item.title: Webex shows how its app uses both iPhone Duo screens
item.description: Cisco says Webex was built natively for iPhone Duo. Opening the phone shows more meeting participants while shared content stays visible, and you can use a whiteboard or run Webex beside another app in Split View. The app is already on the App Store.

item.title: HomeView code hints at chatbot apps and a spoofing lockout
item.description: Code in the iOS 27.3 beta contains a "Conversational Apps" category for HomeView, plus groundwork such as two-way audio routing and interruption handling, which the finder says is not fully wired up. Which apps could use it, or when, is unknown. Separately, HomeView software 27.2 asks for iPhone…

item.title: iPhone Duo launch-day buyers: the return window closes soon
item.description: Apple's return period runs from delivery, not order date. In the US, a Duo delivered on launch day (23 October) can be returned until 6 November; in Canada the deadline is 7 November. In the UK and EU, online buyers have 14 days to tell Apple, then 14 more to send it back. This covers purchases…

item.title: CNET's iPhone Duo fold test passes 260,000 folds
item.description: CNET built a "Fold-a-Phone" machine that has been opening and closing a Duo around the clock for over a week, streamed on YouTube on weekdays from 1 to 5 p.m. ET. It has passed 260,000 folds with no failures reported, and the hinge and crease look to be holding up well. Testing continues daily…

item.title: Safari Technology Preview 256 is out
item.description: Apple's test browser gets another round of bug fixes and performance work, covering areas such as CSS, JavaScript, media, networking, rendering, security, WebGL and WebRTC. It installs through Software Update and runs alongside regular Safari.

item.title: iOS 27.3 will scan public iCloud links for harmful content
item.description: Starting with the 27.3 releases, photos and files shared with 'Anyone with the link' will be checked for things like malware and child abuse material, and Apple can remove flagged items or act on the account. Shares sent to chosen people or as copies aren't checked. Publicly linked content is no…

item.title: Apps can now show offers when you try to cancel a subscription
item.description: Developers can set up retention messages with text, images or special offers in App Store Connect, for subscribers who start cancelling an auto-renewable subscription. A separate Retention Messaging API can pick the message per subscriber, but access is by request only.

item.title: Xcode 27.3 beta adds Copilot, Siri AI testing and touchscreen Mac APIs
item.description: The first Xcode 27.3 beta reached developers on 3 November. MacRumors reports three additions: GitHub Copilot in the built-in coding assistant, a way to test Siri AI integration in apps, and new APIs for the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro. MacRumors lists no system requirements.

item.title: Google Maps now fills both iPhone Duo screens
item.description: Version 26.44.4 removes the black strip that the previous version left beside the status bar. The map now spreads across the inner screen, with search at the upper left, tabs in a left panel and controls on the right. Google’s release notes do not mention Duo.

item.title: macOS 27.3 beta puts Live Activities in the menu bar
item.description: On Apple silicon Macs without a Dynamic Island, Live Activities now appear in the menu bar. Apple Music, Clock, Voice Memos and screen recording are supported, and third-party apps can add support. The update is expected in December.

item.title: iPhone 18e said to be mostly a chip upgrade
item.description: Leaker Fixed Focus Digital says the chip is the only upgrade he can confirm. Earlier, Digital Chat Station claimed an A20 chip, a 6.12-inch 60Hz OLED and one 48-megapixel camera. Spring 2027 launch expected. Neither leaker is confirmed by Apple.

item.title: Non-touch high-end MacBook Pros may be phased out
item.description: Mark Gurman (Bloomberg) questions whether Apple will keep updating the non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models, saying the two lines are likely to merge. He gave no date. M7 Pro and M7 Max touchscreen models are reportedly planned for 2027.

item.title: Safari gets vertical tabs and an adaptive dark mode in the 27.3 betas
item.description: Tabs can now run down the left side of the screen, which suits the iPhone Duo's larger display. A new adaptive Dark Mode darkens bright sites, and Siri can sort and close tabs. Siri understanding full page content comes later. Public release is expected in December.

item.title: Apple Music adds Selfie Sing, a karaoke video mode
item.description: Pick a song, tap the camera icon and record yourself with scrolling lyrics. Afterwards you can add an effect such as Echo or Concert Hall and save or share the clip. The camera option needs the iOS 27.3 beta, and not every song supports it yet.

item.title: Apple Watch Veterans Day challenge returns on 11 November
item.description: Finish any workout of 11 minutes or more on 11 November to earn an award in Fitness, plus animated Messages stickers.

item.title: Researchers jailbreak an iPhone 18 Pro in Lockdown Mode
item.description: Hacker team Calif says its jailbreak got past Lockdown Mode and survived an update to iOS 27.2. It is unclear whether it works on a phone already on 27.2. Calif says it is reporting the bugs to Apple and will not release a public tool. No Apple response has been reported yet.

item.title: iPhone 18 may get a bigger battery and a higher price
item.description: Leaker Digital Chat Station says the standard iPhone 18 gets a larger battery than the iPhone 17’s 3,692 mAh, plus a possible price rise he does not detail. Other claims: 6.3-inch OLED, A20 chip, dual 48-megapixel cameras, first-half 2027 launch.

item.title: iOS 27.3 beta 1 is out, with one-handed Reachability for iPhone Duo
item.description: Apple opened the first iOS 27.3 developer beta. On iPhone Duo, Reachability now works on the outer screen: with the phone closed, a short swipe in from the left or right edge slides the content toward that side. It is on by default and can be switched off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch. The…

item.title: Redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta, with more languages
item.description: Apple says the redesigned Health app is in the iOS 27.3 developer beta and adds language support: Global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish and Vietnamese. It has an Insights tab, a For You section, and a Longevity tab…

item.title: Fitness+ adds Gym Strength plans in beta
item.description: Apple announced Gym Strength in Fitness+: four-week plans built around your goals, experience, schedule and equipment, adjusted each week from the reps and weights you log. It has 350+ exercises across 30+ equipment types. It needs iOS or iPadOS 27.3 (Apple Watch with watchOS 27.3 is optional) and…

item.title: The Verge: iPad mini’s 60Hz OLED screen is a letdown
item.description: David Pierce says the missing 120Hz is not a dealbreaker but he notices it: scrolling text looks blurrier and Apple Pencil feels less smooth. Apple’s reply is that OLED’s fast pixel response reduces motion blur, so a higher refresh rate is not needed. Pierce disagrees.

item.title: Hands-on: OLED iPad mini feels close to a small iPad Pro
item.description: MacRumors highlights the 8.5-inch OLED screen (still 60Hz), the 255 g body, IP67 resistance and 12GB of memory with the A20 Pro. Battery life is rated the same as before. It starts at $699 and arrives November 6.

item.title: Tom's Guide: iPad mini battery beats Apple's claim
item.description: In a single web-browsing test over Wi-Fi, the new iPad mini ran 14 hours 24 minutes, versus 10 hours 36 minutes for the previous model. Apple rates both at up to 10 hours. Tom's Guide completed only one run, so more testing is needed.

item.title: TrendForce: iPhone Duo could take nearly 30% of foldables in 2027
item.description: The research firm forecasts Apple at 24.8% of foldable shipments in 2026 and 29.8% in 2027, with about 5 million Duo units this year. Samsung stays first at 31.9% in 2027. This is a forecast, not an Apple figure.

item.title: MKBHD goes back to iPhone 18 Pro after two weeks with Duo
item.description: Marques Brownlee said on his Waveform podcast that he missed the Pro's cameras and Face ID. He liked opening the foldable, using it in portrait and reading on the larger screen.

item.title: Apple posts a record September quarter: $114.5 billion
item.description: Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion and earnings per share were $2.10, up 14%. Apple reports record iPhone revenue for the quarter, an all-time high for Services and a record $479 billion for the fiscal year. Tariff refunds added about $0.05 to earnings per share.

item.title: Ternus: no end date for iPhone Duo shortages
item.description: Speaking after the earnings report, CEO John Ternus said Apple is supply-constrained on iPhone Duo and can’t predict when supply and demand will balance. Orders placed on earnings day show January delivery estimates. He added that only a very small share of units have been returned over the…

item.title: New tvOS 27.2 build for the updated Apple TV 4K
item.description: Apple released tvOS 27.2 build 24K154 only for the new fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, which launches 13 November at $299. Existing models stay on build 24K122. Apple hasn’t published release notes; one report says the build turns on Siri AI for the new box.

item.title: Dating apps must carry an 18+ rating on the App Store
item.description: From 16 November, developers must say whether their apps include dating or relationship features, including virtual companions with romantic content, and whether they share real-world location. Dating apps will need a minimum 18+ rating (A18 in Brazil). Everyone has until 12 January 2027 to submit…

item.title: Supreme Court will hear Apple’s Epic appeal on 11 January
item.description: Oral arguments are set for 11 January 2027. Apple is appealing the 2025 contempt ruling that said it broke the original injunction by limiting external payment links and charging commission on outside purchases. The court is reviewing only the contempt finding; what Apple may charge is being…

item.title: Apple sends spyware warnings to users in 99 countries
item.description: Apple sent a new round of threat notifications saying some people may have been targeted by mercenary spyware. The Financial Times, as relayed by 9to5Mac, says German officials were among those warned and that the attacks reportedly used a zero-click flaw. Apple does not name who is behind it and…

item.title: iOS 27.2.1 in testing; iOS 27.3 beta due this week
item.description: MacRumors saw iOS 27.2.1 in its visitor logs, likely a small fix update that includes iPhone Duo. Apple’s China newsroom said the iOS 27.3 beta arrives 4 November (likely 3 November in the US), with a public release in December. It turns on some Apple Intelligence features in China, using…

item.title: Apple first planned to launch iPhone Duo in November
item.description: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple originally meant to wait until November and sell the Duo only in the US and China. It instead launched in more than 70 countries on 23 October, with too little stock for demand. Delivery estimates are around 25 January.

item.title: iPhone Duo buyer waits shrink to about 89 days
item.description: UBS Evidence Lab data as of 30 October puts the average Duo wait near 89 days, about a week shorter than the week before. UBS says the screen-crack reports are unlikely to be the main reason, and the data cannot show whether demand fell or supply improved.

item.title: Zoom and Microsoft Office apps now optimized for iPhone Duo
item.description: Zoom shows shared content and participants together on the inner display. Word, PowerPoint, Excel and OneNote have been updated, and Outlook has been optimized since launch. Teams is not yet. Apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later fill both screens.

item.title: Display Zoom can’t be changed after Duo setup
item.description: The Default/Medium/Large text size is chosen during setup, but the usual Settings > Appearance > Display Zoom option is missing afterwards on iOS 27.2. One owner says Apple Support told them the only fix is to erase and set up again. Apple hasn’t commented.

item.title: A robotic HomeView with a 9-inch swiveling screen
item.description: The Information’s Aaron Tilley reports a prototype with a 9-inch display on a swiveling arm that uses cameras and sensors to act on its own, for around $1,000. Apple reportedly hopes for 2027, but it may slip to 2028. The name is unconfirmed.

item.title: HomeView may double as a security camera
item.description: Code sleuth pdfu found settings strings in HomeView software 27.2 describing HomeKit Secure Video camera modes (Off, Detect Activity, Stream, Stream & Allow Recording) with schedules. Apple hasn’t announced a camera feature, and it may not be there at launch on 13 November.
